name: Massachusetts
standard: WCAG 2.1 (or later) A/AA; ATAG 2.0 for authoring tools; Section 508 Ch. 4 + 521 CMR for hardware

laws.summary: Executive department agencies must follow EOTSS IT policies, which is the authority for the Enterprise Digital Accessibility Policy.
Establishes the Digital Accessibility and Equity Governance Board that advises EOTSS on the policy.

laws.cite: 28 CFR Part 35, Subpart H (ADA Title II web & mobile rule, 2024; dates extended by IFR 2026-07663)
laws.summary: Federal floor: state and local government web content and mobile apps must conform to WCAG 2.1 AA; the April 2026 IFR moved compliance to 2027-04-26 (pop. 50,000+) and 2028-04-26 (smaller entities and special districts).

policy_docs.title: Commonwealth Executive Department Digital Accessibility Statement

applies_to: Executive Department offices, boards, commissions and agencies; other entities using EOTSS services (e.g. mass.gov) as a condition of use; contractors building digital assets for them.

deadlines.what: ADA Title II rule: state government and local governments with population 50,000+ must conform web content and mobile apps to WCAG 2.1 AA (extended from 2026-04-24 by DOJ IFR effective 2026-04-20)
ADA Title II rule: local governments under 50,000 and special district governments (extended from 2027-04-26)

requires: Secretariat IT Accessibility Officer implements; agency CIO accountable
Automated and manual testing before deployment and ongoing monitoring
Mitigation Plan for any noncompliant asset, submitted with an exception request
Enterprise digital accessibility statement maintained by EOTSS
mobile: explicit — policy scope lists mobile applications under WCAG 2.1+.
procurement: Must follow 'Procurement of Accessible Digital Products and Services' and use Vendor Digital Accessibility Contract Language (details not reviewed).
enforcement: Noncompliant agencies may lose capital funding eligibility; domain requests denied; EOTSS may remove DNS records of violating assets. Inquiries: digitalaccessibility@mass.gov.
notes: mass.gov returned 403 to direct fetches; policy read from the Wayback Machine 2026 snapshot. No Massachusetts statute setting a web standard found; authority is c.7D plus civil rights laws. Procurement guidance page not opened.
